guarantees.claim: For each share i from 0 to Shares-1, data_truncated[i] is assigned the lower KeyWidth bits of data_i[i].

assumptions.claim: KeyWidth must be less than or equal to the bit width of each element of data_i, otherwise the part-select [KeyWidth-1:0] will be out-of-range and produce X.
assumptions.risk: If KeyWidth > data_i[i] width, data_truncated[i] becomes X, corrupting key material and potentially propagating a silent fault.

uncertain_points.claim: The truncation to KeyWidth bits may discard high-order bits of the key shares. It is unclear whether this is the intended effective key length or if the full share width should be used.
uncertain_points.risk: Key entropy is reduced, potentially weakening cryptographic operations if the truncation is not deliberate and accounted for.
